name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district with a long-tenured incumbent, Jared Huffman, seeking reelection
Huffman holds over $1.1 million in cash while Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No polls or expert ratings flag any vulnerability for the incumbent
model.rationale: Huffman's D+13 district, his million-dollar financial advantage over a challenger with no visible fundraising, and markets pricing his win near 98 percent all point the same way, so the forecast holds a comfortable Democratic margin with no evidence of vulnerability.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Huffman or unexpected polling showing a tighter race would be the main things that could narrow this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 2nd District leans Democratic by thirteen points, and Jared Huffman has held the seat since 2013. He enters the general election with more than $1.1 million on hand, while Republican Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent.

The available evidence points the same direction: the district's partisan lean, Huffman's incumbency advantage, and his financial edge all favor the Democrat. Barring an unexpected development, Huffman is positioned for a comfortable victory in November.
